problem.claim: Understand and manage how training data influences motion in video generation models.

gap.claim: The role of data in influencing motion was poorly understood.

contributions.claim: Motive is a motion-centric, gradient-based data-attribution framework designed to scale to large video datasets and models.
It isolates temporal dynamics from static appearance using motion-weighted loss masks for efficient, motion-specific influence computation.
It uses motion attribution to identify influential fine-tuning clips and guide data curation for text-to-video models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that Motive is, to their knowledge, the first framework to attribute motion rather than visual appearance in video generative models and use that attribution for fine-tuning-data curation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Motive identifies clips strongly affecting motion and guides curation that improves temporal consistency and physical plausibility in text-to-video models.
Using Motive-selected high-influence data, the authors report improved motion smoothness and dynamic degree on VBench, plus a 74.1% human-preference win rate over the pretrained base model.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies limited understanding of how data affects motion in video generation.
It introduces Motive, which computes scalable, motion-specific data influence by separating temporal dynamics from appearance.
Motive is applied to fine-tuning-clip analysis and curation; the authors report better motion-related metrics and human preference than the pretrained base.
The authors characterize the framework as the first, to their knowledge, to attribute motion rather than appearance and use that attribution for curation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly separates temporal dynamics from static appearance with motion-weighted loss masks before computing influence.

lessons.interpretation: Separating entangled objectives can make attribution more targeted and align the analysis with the desired behavior.
lessons.application: For a generative-model analysis, define an objective or mask that isolates the behavior of interest before ranking influential training examples.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the target behavior is inherently coupled to appearance or when the proposed decomposition lacks a meaningful operational definition.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify model sizes, datasets, fine-tuning settings, VBench protocol, human-evaluation design, or comparison baselines beyond the pretrained base.
The reported improvements do not establish independent verification or explain which clips cause which specific motion changes.

editorial_revisions.before: The role of data in influencing motion was poorly understood, especially relative to static visual appearance.
editorial_revisions.after: The role of data in influencing motion was poorly understood.
